items.a: Complete all Training Tracks in the Academy — they teach you the basics of raiding, hacking, bombing, and fleet management. Then head to Intergalactic Chat and ask around for a player-run fleet to join.

A fleet is a group of players who work together. You can join a fleet, contribute units, earn fleet XP, and access fleet assets like the Dyson Sphere and Medical Bay. Having a fleet behind you makes a big difference.

Your home fleet is the fleet you're committed to. You must be in a fleet for 5 consecutive days before it becomes your home fleet. Home fleet members can access fleet assets and participate in fleet activities.
Raid other players! Successful raids steal units from your target. You can also earn units from contracts, daily challenges, faction events, and the Medical Bay.

Total power reflects your combat strength — raid, hack, and bomb power plus your defensive stats and population bonus. It determines your ranking on leaderboards. Upgrade your buildings, level your Gems, and grow your population to increase it.

Raids steal units from another player. Your raid power vs their raid/turret defense determines the outcome. Upgrade your Garrison to increase your raid troop capacity, and keep Enrich active for bigger payouts.
Hacks deal damage to a player's shield. Your hack power vs their firewall power determines the outcome. Once their shield is down (0 HP), they become vulnerable to bombs.

Bombs destroy population — but only if the target's shield is at 0 HP. Your bomb power vs their bombing dome power determines the outcome. Population matters because it boosts your total power and resource production.

When your shield is destroyed, you can instantly restore part of it with the Emergency Shield — it's free (no Federal Crystals) but has a 2-minute cooldown, so use it wisely right after your shield breaks to protect against bombs.

items.q: What happens when my troops run out?
items.a: Troops regenerate slowly over time. You can also spend 100 Federal Crystals to instantly refill ALL three troop types (raid, hack, and bomb) at once. Each attack costs troops whether you win or lose, so plan your attacks carefully.

The Ion Cannon is a long-range weapon that deals damage directly to an enemy's shield (it never touches population). You must charge it with Federal Crystals before firing, and it can't overkill — damage is capped at the target's remaining shield.
Enrich boosts your raid payouts and resource production for 2 hours. Higher Enrich levels increase the bonus. It has a 1-day cooldown — activate it from your own profile before a raiding session.

Fortify temporarily DOUBLES your defensive power across raids, hacks, and bombs, making you much harder to beat. Duration scales with its level (2 hours per level) and it has a 3-day cooldown. Activate it from your own profile when you expect incoming attacks.

Scramble completely deflects ALL incoming bomb damage while it's active (lasts roughly 40–80 minutes). The catch: it zeroes out your hack troops, which won't regenerate while it's running, and Scramble ends the moment you launch an attack of your own. It's a pure defensive shield for your population.

Nullify shuts down another player's active buffs — it cancels their Enrich, Fortify, and Nullify and puts those on cooldown. (It does not cancel Scramble.) You must be at least level 5 to use it, and it has a 7-day cooldown, so save it for a key target.

Faction Games are fast, scheduled team-vs-team PvP wars — two squads battle across a roughly 60-minute match split into timed phases. They're completely separate from Faction Orders (the long points race) and from auto-tracked Fleet Wars. Check the Faction Games screen for the schedule and to sign up.

items.q: What's the difference between a Team War and an Individual War?
items.a: Individual Wars let you sign up solo during the signup window — players are then auto-matched into two balanced teams. Team Wars are pre-formed: a squad captain registers a full roster of teammates to face another squad. The schedule shows which type each upcoming game is.

items.q: How do I sign up and form a team?
items.a: For an Individual War, just tap Sign Up during the signup window. For a Team War, your squad's leader or co-leader submits the full roster before signup closes. To create a squad, pick a name (3–32 characters) and a short tag (2–6 letters/numbers).

items.q: How does energy work in a Faction Game?
items.a: You start each war with 100 energy and regenerate it over time (faster during the mid-war Overdrive phase, and much faster if you're the last one standing on your team). Every action costs energy: Raid 15, Hack 20, Bomb 30, plus smaller costs for abilities and recon. Spend it wisely.

items.q: How do I score points in a Faction Game?
items.a: Knocking out an enemy is worth a huge 1,000 points. Landing attacks earns points too — Hack 25, Raid 20, Bomb 20 — and simply surviving to the end is worth 300. The team with the most total points when the clock runs out (or that eliminates the other team) wins. Note: a successful Scramble reflect protects you but does NOT award points.

items.q: What abilities can I use during a Faction Game?
items.a: In-war powers include Fortify and Bunker Down (halve incoming damage, and they stack), Scramble (one-time use per war — reflects up to 5 incoming attacks back at the attackers' team, active until all 5 are used), Shield Relay (restores shield HP), Rally and Counter-Rally (damage buffs / cleanse), and Recon (scout an enemy's stats). Each costs energy and has its own cooldown.

items.q: What do I get for winning?
items.a: Everyone on the winning team earns 500 Federal Crystals; the losing team still gets 200. The match MVP earns a bonus 250 on top. Your wins, losses, streaks, and lifetime stats are tracked in your Faction Games history.

The War Pass is a seasonal reward track fueled by Faction Games: you earn 50 points for participating in a war and 100 points for winning one. Climb the point tiers to claim rewards — including exclusive starship skins at the top.

items.q: I switched squads — can my new squad still sign me up?
items.a: Yes. If an old squad had already put you on a war roster, signing up with your new squad automatically releases you from the stale roster. Players who are genuinely on another squad's active roster for that war can't be double-signed.
The Frontlines is a cooperative PvE system where deployed players work together to take down NPC Coalition fleets. Deploy from the Intel tab in Archives to participate.
Go to Archives → Intel and tap Deploy to Frontlines. Once deployed you can attack NPC targets. You can withdraw at any time, but there's a 1-hour cooldown before you can redeploy.

items.q: How does the siege system work?
items.a: Each NPC has four phases: Supplies → Shields → Hull → Boarding. Raid their supplies down, hack their shields, bomb their hull, then raid again to board and destroy them. All deployed players contribute damage together.

When an NPC's hull reaches 0, a timed boarding window opens — everyone must raid its core systems before the timer runs out. The window length depends on the NPC's tier (about 4 hours for the easiest down to 15 minutes for the toughest). If it expires, the NPC repairs its hull and you have to bomb it down again.

Yes — but specifically when your fleet takes on a PvP Operative Contract. While that contract is active, the targeted Coalition fleet launches retaliatory strikes against your fleet members. Make sure your defenses are strong before you start one.

items.q: What happens when I destroy an NPC?
items.a: You earn XP scaled to the NPC's difficulty tier, and your damage is recorded on the contribution leaderboard. When every member of an NPC fleet is destroyed, the fleet is neutralized.

Contracts are PvE missions made up of stages, each with Raid, Hack, and/or Bomb bars to deplete. Clear all the stages to earn a unit payout for your fleet, plus faction-order points and battle-pass progress. Longer multi-stage contracts pay a bonus.

items.q: What rank do I need to start a contract?
items.a: Any rank above the entry tier can start contracts — only Recruits and Cadets cannot. Everyone from Operative/Sentry upward is eligible. (You can join in on a contract your fleet has already started regardless.)

items.q: My troops keep running out during contracts!
items.a: Use 100 Federal Crystals to instantly refill all three troop types, or let them regenerate over time. Plan your attacks to use raid, hack, and bomb troops efficiently across the bars.

Also called Hunter's Mandate, these are special red contracts that appear at the top of your Available Contracts list. Instead of a generic target, you hunt one specific Coalition operative who's at full strength. Tap the contract to view that operative's profile, then coordinate with your fleet to eliminate them.

items.q: How often do PvP Operative Contracts appear, and what do they pay?
items.a: A new offer can arrive as often as every 3 hours, with no weekly limit — but only one at a time, so finish or let one expire before the next can arrive. An offer expires if not started within 48 hours. Rewards scale with your personal contribution to the kill — units based on damage dealt, a Federal Crystal payout (minimum 100), and a graded Colony Pod bonus for the top 5 contributors (5 pods for 1st place down to 1 for 5th) that deploys instantly as population and power — plus faction-order points. Warning: starting one provokes retaliation from the enemy fleet against your whole fleet.

items.q: How is my PvP Operative target chosen?
items.a: Targets are matched to your fleet's strength — stronger fleets draw tougher operatives, and every offer card shows an honest difficulty badge: Easy, Medium, Hard, or Very Hard, based on the target's actual defenses. Tougher targets take more damage to bring down, which also means bigger payouts. Echo announces new offers, starts, and kills in your fleet chat.

Every combat building (Garrison, Penetration Team, Bombing Bay) commands its own territory of 20 Lands. Tap ENTER on the building in the Upgrades screen to visit its Lands, develop structures on each plot, and grow the building's power beyond its normal cap.

Each Land levels from 1 to 10 using units, and every level adds power split between attack and defense for that building. Land attack raises your raid/hack/bomb attack, and land defense raises the matching defense — both show on your profile's combat cards.

items.q: Do Lands give any other bonuses?
items.a: Yes — your total land ATTACK power sharpens your offense beyond raw stats: it boosts your contract damage (all attack types), your raid plunder, and your bomb damage by up to +30% with fully developed all-attack lands. Land upgrades also earn faction-order points for the units spent.

Four objectives your whole fleet completes together each day (UTC): members logging in, Fleet XP donations, different members talking in fleet chat, and units spent on upgrades. Targets scale with your fleet's size. Track progress on the Fleet screen or ask '@Echo dailies' in fleet chat.

items.q: What do we get for completing all four?
items.a: Your fleet instantly unlocks Operation Daybreak — an exclusive T6 contract paying 150% plunder — at the top of Available Contracts. You have until the END of the next day (00:00 UTC reset) to start it, so an early completion gives you up to ~47 hours.

Complete every daily from Sunday through Friday and on Saturday your fleet is granted Operation Daybreak: Overdrive — a massive 20-stage T6 campaign with boss stages and a mountain of plunder. Miss a single day and the Overdrive waits for next week, so keep the streak alive!
The Medical Bay is a fleet asset that rescues a portion of your population when you get bombed. Instead of being destroyed permanently, some civilians are moved to triage in the Medical Bay.
It depends on your fleet's Medical Bay level — higher levels rescue more, with both a per-player cap and a fleet-wide capacity. Upgrade it to protect more of your population from bombing.

items.q: How do I recover my triage population?
items.a: Open the Medical Bay in your fleet assets and revive your patients. Reviving with units costs 40% of the normal population cost, or you can use a Nano Serum item to revive everyone for free.
Yes — patients only stay in triage for a limited time. If you don't revive them in time, they're lost permanently, so check the Medical Bay soon after getting bombed.

items.q: Does every fleet have a Medical Bay?
items.a: No — it must be purchased as a fleet asset by fleet leadership. If your fleet doesn't have one, your destroyed population is lost immediately.
Fleet assets are major infrastructure that benefit your entire home fleet — the Dyson Sphere, Halo Vault, Sentry Swarm, Medical Bay, and more. Only home fleet members can access their benefits.

items.q: How do I get fleet assets?
items.a: Top fleet leadership (Generals, Sovereigns, and Admirals) can purchase assets from the Fleet Assets screen using units from the Fleet Vault. Different assets unlock at different fleet levels.

items.q: How do I upgrade fleet assets?
items.a: Generals, Sovereigns, and Admirals can upgrade assets up to Level 5. Each upgrade costs units from the Fleet Vault and improves the asset's benefits.

items.q: How does my fleet earn Fleet XP?
items.a: Two ways: daily donations (each member can donate 2,500 units once a day for +25 Fleet XP — the most XP-efficient path), and big infrastructure spending — buying or upgrading fleet assets grants Fleet XP based on the units spent, announced by Echo in fleet chat. Fleet XP levels your fleet up to Level 10, unlocking more assets and member slots.

items.q: When does the Fleet Store restock?
items.a: Every Monday at 00:00 UTC, all limited-stock Fleet Store items reset to full stock — Echo announces it in fleet chat. Ask '@Echo store' anytime to see your fleet's current stock and the restock countdown.
Federal Crystals are the premium currency. Use them to charge the Ion Cannon, instantly regenerate troops, and more. Earn them from contracts, daily challenges, faction events, and the Traders Hall.
Gems boost your combat stats permanently. Gem of Destruction boosts bomb power, Gem of Technology boosts hack power, and Gem of Power boosts raid power. Level them up in the Traders Hall.

items.q: What do the different items do?
items.a: Repair Kit — helps recover from EMP damage. Colony Pod — instantly adds population. Architect's Blueprint — grants 92 combat XP that YOU allocate between raid, hack, and bomb using the sliders when you use it. Knowledge Crystal — grants player XP toward your level. Nano Serum — revives all Medical Bay patients for free. Collect them from the Traders Hall, events, and rewards.

items.q: Can I use multiple Knowledge Crystals at once?
items.a: Yes — pick a quantity when you use them. Each crystal has a chance to CRIT for a 5× XP burst, and a chance to trigger a Wisdom Broadcast that grants bonus XP to every member of your fleet. Bulk sessions make those lucky rolls add up.

items.q: Why does population cost more the more I have?
items.a: Population uses tiered pricing — your first 120,000 pop costs 1 unit each, and the price per unit doubles at each tier above that (2 at 120K, 4 at 240K, 8 at 360K, and so on). This keeps high-population players from snowballing endlessly.

Faction Orders are 15-day campaigns where you earn points just by playing — raids, hacks, bombs, and contract completions all count. Hit point thresholds to claim tiered rewards (units, crystals, and items) for yourself.
There are two layers: tiered rewards you claim as you pass point thresholds, and end-of-campaign placement rewards (Federal Crystals and Colony Pods) for the top 3 players in each faction.
The player with the most Faction Order points when the campaign ends is crowned the Galactic Champion, earning special recognition and a crown for a limited time.

The Battle Pass is a seasonal progression track with rewards you unlock as you earn Battle Pass XP through normal play. There's a free track everyone can claim and a premium track that unlocks extra rewards at each tier.

items.q: How do I make progress on the Battle Pass?
items.a: Complete the Battle Pass weekly challenges to earn XP and climb tiers. Each tier hands out rewards like units, crystals, XP, and items. Claim your free and premium rewards from the Battle Pass screen as you unlock them.

items.q: Can I gift the Battle Pass to another player?
items.a: Yes! Visit their profile and tap the 🎁 Gift Pass button in Player Actions — it costs the same as buying it for yourself, and the pass activates on their account instantly. The button only appears if they don't already own the current pass.

Daily Challenges are quick objectives that reset every day — things like winning a number of raids or hacks. Complete them and submit to collect rewards such as Federal Crystals and units. Check back daily for a fresh set.

The Starship Bay lets you customize your personal flagship — hull, paint colors, finish, decals, backdrop, and glow effects like rim and engine glow. It's purely cosmetic and shows off on your profile.

items.q: How do I customize my starship?
items.a: Open your profile and tap your starship card to enter the Starship Bay. Tapping another player's starship lets you inspect their design.
An EMP (Electromagnetic Pulse) is a fleet-level attack that disrupts a target player, preventing their shield from being repaired normally. While under an EMP, you cannot simply restore your shield.

items.q: How do I recover from an EMP?
items.a: EMPs last for a set duration. Your fleet members can send Repair Kits to help you recover faster. Once the timer expires or enough help arrives, your shield becomes repairable again.

Fleet wars are tracked conflicts between two fleets. When members of opposing fleets attack each other, the damage is recorded in the war stats. View active wars in the Archives → Wars tab. (These are separate from the scheduled Faction Games team battles.)
Wars begin automatically when fleets rack up significant combat activity against each other. They track raid wins, shield damage dealt, population destroyed, and more.

Commendations are your medal wall — 50+ commander medals for raids, hacks, bombs, garrison wipes, building levels, leaderboard rank, and more, plus fleet commendations your whole crew earns together. Tap the 🏅 button on your profile to see them, with live progress bars toward every unearned medal.

items.q: Do fleet commendations disappear if our stats drop?
items.a: No — fleet commendations are sticky. Once your fleet earns one (say, reaching the top 10 by power), it's kept forever, even if the requirement is no longer met later.
The garrison-destroyer commendations count the times you've raided an enemy's garrison all the way down to 0 troops in a winning raid — a total wipe of their defenders.

items.q: What can I ask Echo in fleet chat?
items.a: Type '@Echo' followed by a command in fleet chat: 'dailies' (live Fleet Dailies progress), 'war' (the current or next Faction Games war), 'store' (Fleet Store stock and restock timer), 'space' (open roster spots), or 'help' for the full menu. Everyone can use these.

Yes — fleet officers (Commander and above) can use '@Echo announce <message>' to send a full fleet announcement (with the popup for offline members) and '@Echo defcon <1-5>' to set the fleet's readiness level from chat. Echo politely refuses anyone below the required rank.
An ambassador code is a unique code assigned to content creators and community leaders. You can enter an ambassador code in Settings to show your support for them.

items.q: How do I support an ambassador?
items.a: Go to Settings → Administration → Support an Ambassador. Enter their code and tap Set. You can change your ambassador at any time.

items.q: How do I get my own ambassador code?
items.a: Ambassador codes are assigned to recognized content creators and community leaders. If you're actively creating content or leading a community for Galactic Conquest, reach out on Discord to learn more.

items.q: Does using a referral code set my ambassador automatically?
items.a: Yes — if the player who referred you has an ambassador code, you'll automatically be set as supporting them when you create your account. You can change this anytime in Settings.

items.q: How do I change my username?
items.a: Go to Settings and tap Change Username. You can change your name once every 7 days. Capitalization changes are allowed. Your progress, fleet membership, and all data carry over.

items.q: How do I recover my account on a new phone?
items.a: Use the Reclaim Account option on the login screen. Enter the email and password you set up when you created your account. If you forgot your password, use the Reset Password option to receive a reset code via email.

items.q: I forgot my password, how do I reset it?
items.a: Tap Reset Password on the login screen. Enter the email associated with your account and you'll receive a 6-digit code. Enter the code and set a new password, then use Reclaim Account to log in.
No. Emulators and automated tools are not supported and will be blocked. Galactic Conquest is designed for mobile devices only.

items.q: I'm experiencing lag or connection issues
items.a: Try closing and reopening the app. If the issue persists, check your internet connection. The game uses WebSocket connections that can sometimes drop on unstable networks.

items.q: How do I join the Discord?
items.a: Join our community Discord at discord.gg/gu7R5hp4 — report bugs, suggest features, and connect with other commanders!
